title: Toward generalizable and interpretable AI in regulatory genomics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC flags show no open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no data or database cross-references, no text-mined accessions, and no Zenodo/Dryad hits. The two NCBI PMC links returned (13596691, 13081850) are linked records, not this paper's data. No data files exist to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (full text paywalled). The abstract states this is a Review of sequence-to-function models (models that predict regulatory readouts from DNA sequence); it describes no new measurements or dataset.

a1_downloadable.note: Review article; no dataset deposited or linked. Checked Europe PMC flags, NCBI links and repository search: nothing found.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No data table exists, so there is no label column; any project would have to assemble labels from other papers' datasets.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs provided; paper only surveys others' data.

honest_claim_h3: None: the paper is a review with no data of its own, so no model claim can rest on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence to predict gene-regulatory activity across genetic variants and cell types, testing how well predictions generalize.
plain_idea.train_on: Nothing from this paper: it is a review and supplies no examples (count unknown / zero).
plain_idea.predict: Regulatory readouts such as chromatin accessibility or expression would have to come from other papers' assays, not from this one.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: The review flags poor generalization across variants and cell contexts as the open problem, which could point to a project, but the data must be found elsewhere.

label_elsewhere.why: No dataset in this paper to extend.

ml_idea: None from this paper. The review's named gap (sequence-to-function models generalize poorly across individuals' genetic variation and across cell contexts) is a lead to follow in primary datasets, such as massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs, experiments that measure the regulatory activity of thousands of DNA fragments at once), not a project here.

effort.compute_note: No data, so nothing to estimate.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the paper deposits any data: it does not (no PMCID, no supplement, no accessions).

verdict_reason: Paywalled Review article with no dataset, supplement or accessions; fails A1 and A2. Its stated open problem (generalizing across variants and cell contexts) is worth following in primary datasets instead.
